66:3.devotion: Near the close of Isaiah, God confronts people who kept up religious routines while their hearts were far from Him. Sacrifices offered without obedience or humility become hollow, even offensive. God looks for hearts that choose His ways, not just rituals that keep up appearances.
66:3.reflection: Are there religious habits in my life that continue while my heart has quietly drifted away from God?
66:3.action: Examine one routine devotion or church practice today, and ask God to renew its meaning rather than simply going through the motions.
66:3.prayer: Lord, search my heart. I do not want my worship to be empty routine. Show me where I have chosen my own ways, and draw me back to delight in You above all else. Amen.

66:4.devotion: God describes the sorrowful result of ignored invitations. He called, and the people did not answer; He spoke, and they did not listen. Persistent refusal to hear God brings real consequences. This passage warns us to respond when God speaks, not to assume there will always be another chance.
66:4.reflection: When God has been nudging me through Scripture, conscience, or circumstances, have I been answering or delaying?
66:4.action: Identify one thing you sense God has been asking of you, and take a first obedient step toward it today.
66:4.prayer: Father, forgive me for the times You called and I did not answer. Give me a soft, responsive heart that listens when You speak and obeys without delay. Amen.

66:5.devotion: Isaiah speaks comfort to the faithful remnant who tremble at God's word. They were rejected and mocked by their own countrymen, even in the name of religion. God assures them that those who cast them out for His sake will ultimately be put to shame, while the faithful are honored.
66:5.reflection: When I face criticism or exclusion for standing with God, do I remember that He sees and vindicates His people?
66:5.action: If someone has rejected or ridiculed you for your faith, release the hurt to God in prayer instead of retaliating today.
66:5.prayer: Lord, You know the sting of being misunderstood and cast out for Your sake. Help me trust Your justice, love those who oppose me, and rest in the honor You give the faithful. Amen.

66:6.devotion: The prophet hears commotion from the city and a voice from the temple—the voice of the LORD who repays His enemies fully. In context, God's judgment was coming upon the unfaithful in Jerusalem itself. The verse reminds us that God is not indifferent to rebellion; He acts with perfect justice in His own time.
66:6.reflection: Do I trust God's justice when wrong seems to go unpunished, or am I tempted to take judgment into my own hands?
66:6.action: Write down one situation of injustice that troubles you, and commit it to God in prayer, choosing to trust His timing.
66:6.prayer: Righteous Lord, You see every wrong and judge with perfect fairness. When injustice disturbs me, teach me to wait on You, to act justly myself, and to leave vengeance in Your hands. Amen.

66:7.devotion: Isaiah uses a striking image of a mother giving birth before labor pains began. This unusual picture belongs to his prophecy of Zion's astonishing restoration, which God would bring about suddenly and unexpectedly. It prepares the reader for verses 8 and 9, where a nation is born in a single day.
66:7.reflection: Where might God be working in ways so sudden and surprising that I have not even thought to ask Him for it?
66:7.action: Thank God in prayer today for one unexpected blessing or answered prayer you received in a way you did not anticipate.
66:7.prayer: God of wonders, You are not bound by my expectations. Open my eyes to Your surprising work around me, and keep me from limiting what I believe You can do. Amen.

66:8.devotion: The prophet asks in amazement: can a land be born in one day, a nation delivered at once? What seems impossible to us, God accomplished for Zion in His restoring mercy. The verse celebrates that God's restoration can arrive suddenly and completely, beyond normal human expectation.
66:8.reflection: Do I believe God can bring restoration quickly and completely in situations I have almost given up on?
66:8.action: Choose one situation you consider hopeless and pray over it today, specifically asking God to work in His way and timing.
66:8.prayer: Lord of the impossible, You bring new life where none seems possible. Strengthen my faith when I am weary, and help me hope in Your power to restore. Amen.

66:9.devotion: God asks two rhetorical questions: would He bring a mother to the time of birth and then fail to deliver? Would He open the womb and then shut it? The answer is clearly no. Having begun His work of restoring His people, God will carry it through to completion.
66:9.reflection: Am I trusting that the good work God has begun in my life and in His church will be carried to completion?
66:9.action: Recall one way God has been working in your life over time, and thank Him today for His faithfulness to finish what He starts.
66:9.prayer: Faithful God, thank You that You do not abandon Your work halfway. When I grow impatient or discouraged, remind me that You complete what You begin. Keep me trusting You. Amen.

66:10.devotion: God invites all who love Jerusalem—and especially all who have mourned over her—to rejoice with her in her restoration. Shared joy is commanded here: the community of faith is called to celebrate God's work together, and those who grieved are specifically included in the invitation to be glad.
66:10.reflection: Do I celebrate the blessings and restoration God brings to others, or does envy and discouragement keep me from rejoicing with them?
66:10.action: Reach out to someone today who has experienced God's blessing or recovery, and congratulate or encourage them genuinely.
66:10.prayer: Lord, give me a heart that rejoices with those who rejoice and mourns with those who mourn. Free me from envy, and let me celebrate every good work You do in others. Amen.

66:11.devotion: Isaiah's final chapter pictures Jerusalem as a nurturing mother. God promises that His restored people will not merely survive but be nourished, satisfied, and delighted. The image of feeding and drinking deeply speaks of a comfort so abundant that it fills the hungriest soul completely.
66:11.reflection: Where am I seeking satisfaction, and am I letting God's comfort truly nourish me?
66:11.action: Set aside ten quiet minutes today to bring one specific hunger of your heart to God in prayer instead of distracting yourself from it.
66:11.prayer: Father, You know the empty places in me. Feed me with Your consolation and let me be satisfied in You alone. Teach me to drink deeply of Your comfort and to find delight in Your presence. Amen.

66:12.devotion: God promises peace extended like a river and glory like a flowing stream. The tender picture of a child carried on the side and dandled on the knees shows that God's peace is not distant or abstract; it is intimate, personal care from a Lord who holds His people close.
66:12.reflection: Do I believe God's care for me is as tender as a parent holding a child on their knees?
66:12.action: Write down one area where you need peace, then picture God's peace flowing to it like a river as you pray over it today.
66:12.prayer: Lord, extend Your peace into my life like a river that keeps flowing. Where I feel anxious or unsteady, carry me as a father carries his child. Let me rest on Your knees and trust Your tender hold. Amen.

66:13.devotion: God speaks through Isaiah to His people, promising a comfort as tender and intimate as a mother's embrace. This is the Lord Himself drawing near to the weary. The promise also points to a place—Jerusalem—where His restored people will know His consolation fully, together.
66:13.reflection: When did you last let God comfort you the way a loving mother soothes her child?
66:13.action: Reach out today to someone who is grieving or discouraged, offering a kind word, a listening ear, or a simple act of care.
66:13.prayer: Father, thank You for comforting me with a mother's tenderness. Draw near to my weary heart today, and make me an instrument of Your consolation to those around me who are hurting.

66:14.devotion: When God's people see His promises fulfilled, their hearts rejoice and even their bones flourish like green grass. This verse contrasts two responses to God's hand: servants who know Him in joy, and enemies who meet His opposition. The invitation is to be among those who rejoice.
66:14.reflection: When I look at what God has done, does my heart actually rejoice, or do I rush past it?
66:14.action: List three ways God's hand has been real in your life this year, and thank Him for each one out loud today.
66:14.prayer: Lord, open my eyes to see Your hand at work around me. Make my heart rejoice and my whole being flourish in Your goodness. Keep me close to You as Your servant, delighting in what You do. Amen.

66:15.devotion: Isaiah portrays the Lord's coming in awesome power, with fire and whirlwind imagery expressing His holy anger against evil. Ancient prophetic language uses these pictures to show that God is not indifferent to wrongdoing; He will act decisively against it. This calls for reverent awe, not terror for those who trust Him.
66:15.reflection: Do I take God's holiness seriously, or have I grown casual about evil in and around me?
66:15.action: Choose one habit, attitude, or compromise you have excused, and name it honestly to God today in confession.
66:15.prayer: Holy God, You are not indifferent to evil, and I should not be either. Search my heart, expose what needs to change, and give me reverence for Your holiness and gratitude for Your patience with me. Amen.

66:16.devotion: This sobering verse declares that the Lord Himself will judge all flesh by fire and sword. Judgment belongs to God alone, not to us. For believers, the verse is a reminder to live with humility and urgency, entrusting justice to the Lord rather than taking vengeance into our own hands.
66:16.reflection: Am I leaving judgment to God, or am I nursing a desire to repay those who have wronged me?
66:16.action: Identify one grievance you are still carrying, and consciously release the outcome of it to God in prayer today.
66:16.prayer: Righteous Lord, You alone see all things and judge fairly. I release my grudges and my need for repayment into Your hands. Help me live humbly, forgive freely, and trust Your justice instead of my own. Amen.

66:17.devotion: God confronts people who performed outward rituals of purification while secretly pursuing idols and forbidden practices. Their religion was a cover for divided hearts. The verse warns that God sees through empty spirituality; He desires genuine devotion, not appearances managed for others to see.
66:17.reflection: Is there any part of my worship that is outward show while my heart is chasing something else?
66:17.action: Examine your private life honestly today and align one hidden habit with what you publicly profess before God.
66:17.prayer: Lord, You know my works and my thoughts. Forgive me for the times my devotion has been a mask. Purify my heart, not just my appearance, and make my whole life honestly devoted to You. Amen.

66:18.devotion: God declares that He knows every work and thought, and yet His purpose reaches beyond judgment to a worldwide gathering. People of every nation and language will come and see His glory. Even a chapter of sober warnings ends with the sweeping reach of God's glory to all peoples.
66:18.reflection: Do I see God's heart as big enough to include people very different from me?
66:18.action: Pray by name for one person or people group far from you, asking God to reveal His glory to them.
66:18.prayer: Lord of all nations and tongues, Your glory is meant for every people on earth. Widen my heart to match Your mission, and use my prayers, words, and kindness to point others toward seeing Your glory. Amen.

66:19.devotion: God promises to send messengers to distant nations that have never heard His fame or seen His glory, and they will declare His glory among the Gentiles. From the start, God's plan included the far coastlands. Those who witness His work become bearers of it to places it has not yet reached.
66:19.reflection: Who in my circle has never really heard of God's glory, and what keeps me from telling them?
66:19.action: Share one specific way God has been faithful to you with one person today, in person or by message.
66:19.prayer: Lord, You send Your people to places that have not heard Your fame. Make me willing to be sent, whether across the street or far away. Use my simple testimony to declare Your glory to someone today. Amen.

66:20.devotion: In Isaiah's closing vision, God pictures people from every nation bringing His scattered children back to Jerusalem, the way worshipers carried offerings in clean vessels. The astonishing image is that people themselves become the offering—brothers and sisters delivered and presented to the Lord as something precious and holy.
66:20.reflection: Who might God be calling me to help carry toward Him today?
66:20.action: Reach out to one person who has drifted from faith, offering a ride, a call, or a meal that gently draws them toward God's house.
66:20.prayer: Lord, use me as a clean vessel. Let my life help carry others into Your presence, and make me willing to be brought near to You myself. Amen.

66:21.devotion: This verse continues the vision of restoration. God declares He will take some of those gathered from the nations and make them priests and Levites—servants once reserved for one family now opened wide. The promise points to a day when access to God's service extends far beyond old boundaries.
66:21.reflection: Do I believe God can call and use people I would never expect?
66:21.action: Encourage someone exploring serving at church, especially someone whose background differs from yours, affirming that God calls unlikely people.
66:21.prayer: Gracious God, thank You for widening Your invitation. Open my eyes to those You are calling, and help me welcome servants You choose, not only the ones I expect. Amen.

66:22.devotion: God anchors His promise in His own faithfulness: as surely as the new heavens and new earth will endure before Him, so will His people and their name. Human kingdoms fade, but the identity God gives His people is secured by His unchanging character and enduring new creation.
66:22.reflection: Where am I placing my sense of security—in what fades or in what God says will remain?
66:22.action: Write down one fear about the future and beside it write God's promise to keep those who are His, then thank Him for it aloud.
66:22.prayer: Faithful God, everything around me feels temporary, but You promise Your people will remain before You. Steady my heart on Your enduring word today. Amen.

66:23.devotion: The vision ends with all flesh—people from every place—coming to worship before the Lord, rhythm after rhythm, month after month, Sabbath after Sabbath. Worship is pictured not as an occasional event but as the steady heartbeat of restored life in God's presence.
66:23.reflection: Is worship a rhythm woven through my ordinary week, or only something I attend?
66:23.action: Set three brief pauses in today's schedule to stop, acknowledge God, and thank Him for something specific.
66:23.prayer: Lord of all nations, teach me to worship with a steady rhythm, not just on special occasions. Draw all people to Yourself, and keep my heart turning toward You. Amen.

66:24.devotion: Isaiah's final image contrasts the enduring worshipers with the fate of those who persistently defied God—a sober picture of lasting judgment, echoing imagery of refuse outside the city. It is a solemn warning, not a cause for triumph: God takes rebellion seriously, and His invitation to worship is urgently good news.
66:24.reflection: Am I treating God's warnings about persistent rebellion as seriously as His promises?
66:24.action: Prayerfully examine one area where you have been resisting God, and confess it honestly today rather than leaving it unaddressed.
66:24.prayer: Holy God, Your warnings are mercy that calls me back before it is too late. Keep me from hardening my heart, and draw me quickly into Your grace. Amen.
